title: Cocoa-Espresso Brisket Rub
description: A finely ground, salt-free blend of cocoa, espresso and coriander gives covered brisket braises a deep peppery flavor.

steps.title: Sift the cocoa
steps.text: Sift {cocoa} and {espresso} into a small dry bowl, pressing any clumps through with a spoon.

steps.title: Blend the seasonings
steps.text: Stir in {paprika}, {garlic}, {coriander} and {pepper} for about 30 seconds until the color is even.

steps.title: Portion the rub
steps.text: Portion about a teaspoon per serving. For a moist brisket braise, stir the measured seasoning into the braising liquid before covering the meat.

notes: Make ahead: Store the dry blend in a tightly sealed jar in a cool cupboard for up to 2 months for best flavor. Measure with a clean dry spoon before handling meat. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. This dry blend stores well in a cupboard; condensation can clump the cocoa. Fridge reheat: Use the dry blend directly. If refrigerated, let the sealed jar come to room temperature before opening. Freezer reheat: If already frozen, bring the still-sealed jar to room temperature before opening and stir out lumps; no heating is needed. Option A uses espresso and black pepper. For gentler Option B, omit the espresso, halve the pepper and use extra sweet paprika to keep a similar yield.
